basis: Mucocutaneous and GI hamartomas are diagnostic features; benign thyroid lesions occur in ~50–70%. Neurodevelopmental damage is not established at ≥30% across the umbrella; cancer risks excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral papillomas and gastrointestinal hamartomas are major diagnostic features.
decisions.neurologic: none: macrocephaly alone is not damage; neurodevelopmental disability is not established in ≥30% across the full PHTS umbrella.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: benign structural thyroid lesions, including adenomas and multinodular disease, occur in approximately 50–70%.

basis: Severe Zellweger disease defines metabolic and neurologic dysfunction; hepatic disease affects most and damaging ocular disease commonly ≥30%. Skeletal stippling and hearing loss omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: profound developmental impairment, neonatal hypotonia and seizures are defining manifestations of severe Zellweger disease.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental disease with neuropathy; optic atrophy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each occur in 3/8. Frequent amyotrophy does not establish direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent lower-limb amyotrophy accompanies axonal neuropathy; direct myopathy or an independent structural muscle disorder is not established.

basis: Aortic aneurysm and skeletal connective-tissue disease define the syndrome; gingival overgrowth affects 2/3. Proptosis and ventriculomegaly alone do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: gingival overgrowth is direct structural involvement of the gums, reported in 2/3 patients (~67%).

basis: Hepatic heme-metabolism disorder defined clinically by neurovisceral attacks or childhood encephalopathy. Ocular disease belongs mainly to rare biallelic forms.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neuropathic neurovisceral attacks and biallelic developmental encephalopathy are defining disease manifestations, rather than later complications.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia, developmental impairment (29/29) and airway obstruction (16/17) are defining features. Hearing loss occurs in 30–79%; dental and skin abnormalities omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: characteristic airway malformations and obstruction are major defining features; obstruction occurs in 16/17 patients.
decisions.neurologic: primary: global developmental delay (29/29) and intellectual disability (16/16) are core features of the syndrome.

basis: Severe intellectual disability, microcephaly and strabismus define the syndrome; strabismus is reported in 80–99%. Short stature alone adds no skeletal axis.

decisions.ocular: primary: strabismus is explicitly part of the defining clinical association and occurs in 80–99%, supporting intrinsic ocular alignment dysfunction.

basis: Cowden mucocutaneous hamartomas include skin and oral lesions. Thyroid involvement ≥30% is not established for this KLLN subtype; cancer predispositions alone add no organs.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the record supplies no thyroid phenotype or frequency; the usual PTEN-associated Cowden thyroid frequency cannot confidently be assigned to this KLLN subtype.

basis: Hypothalamic hamartoma with defining seizures and endocrine dysfunction; polydactyly occurs in 2/2 annotated syndromic cases. Other malformations lack usable frequencies.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: central precocious puberty and hypothalamic endocrine dysfunction are explicitly defining clinical presentations in the supplied definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: postaxial polydactyly occurs in 2/2 annotated patients, with syndactyly in 1/2; these are direct skeletal malformations.

basis: Complete or partial XY gonadal dysgenesis entails impaired testicular endocrine differentiation. Perineal hypospadias is a congenital urethral defect in 2/5 (40%); cardiac ancestry is unsupported.

decisions.renal: involved: perineal hypospadias affects 2/5 patients (40%) and directly malforms the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the complete/partial gonadal dysgenesis parents establish defective testicular endocrine differentiation, beyond an isolated external genital malformation.
